THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

ORDER Petitioners have been charge sheeted for the offence under sections 34 and 498A of IPC, alleging that, the defacto complainant is the legally wedded wife of accused No.1, accused No.2 and accused No.3 are the parents-in-laws, accused No.4 is the sister-in-law, and they subjected respondent No.2 to cruelty both mentally and physically.
The cognizance of the aforesaid offence taken by the learned Magistrate is impugned in this petition.

2. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that, in a petition filed by the defacto complainant under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act, parties have amicably settled the matter, and as per the terms of the settlement, the defacto complainant has agreed to withdraw the impugned proceedings.

Hence, he submits that, the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the petitioners- accused will be an abuse of process of law in view of the settlement arrived Mr Syed Virasat Ali vs State Of Karnataka on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55893474/
2 between the parties.

sentences.text: 3. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 does not dispute that, the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves, and as per the terms of settlement, the defacto complainant has agreed to withdraw the impugned proceedings.
4. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

5. Perusal of the memorandum of settlement between the parties indicates that, the defacto complainant has undertaken to withdraw the impugned proceedings initiated against the petitioners-accused herein, and the marriage of the accused No.1 with the defacto complainant was dissolved under the Muslim Personal Law.

6. Though the offences alleged are cognizable and non-compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that, the accused No.1 and the defacto complainant have amicably settled the dispute between themselves, it will be a futile exercise to continue the criminal proceedings, since the probability of conviction of the petitioners-accused herein is remote and bleak in view of the settlement arrived between the parties.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The criminal petition is allowed;
ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.51464/2018, on the file of the 43rd ACMM,
Mayo Hall, Bengaluru is hereby quashed.
Sd/-
